references.text: Satan entered into Judas. In [ref:Joh 13:2|John 13:2] we read that the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas Iscariot to betray Jesus, and in [ref:Joh 13:27|John 13:27] it says that Satan entered him at the Last Supper.

After the temptation in the wilderness, the devil left Jesus "until a suitable time" ([ref:Luk 4:13|Luke 4:13]). Judas' betrayal marks that Satan now returns to attack Jesus again through one of his own disciples.
Jesus had already said early on that one of the twelve was a devil ([ref:Joh 6:70-71|John 6:70-71]), and he referred to Judas Iscariot, who would betray him.

In [ref:Matt 26:14-16|Matthew 26:14-16] it is described how Judas Iscariot went to the chief priests and agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, which parallels what happens after Satan entered into Judas.
Mark's parallel account of how Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus ([ref:Mark 14:10-11|Mark 14:10-11]).

Judas Iscariot is already mentioned at the selection of the twelve apostles as the one who would become a traitor ([ref:Luk 6:16|Luke 6:16]). Luke emphasizes that he was "one of the twelve", making the betrayal all the more tragic.

In [ref:1 Krøn 21:1|1 Chronicles 21:1] Satan incited David to count Israel. This shows a pattern in Scripture where Satan influences people to act against God's will, just as he here enters Judas to betray Jesus.

Peter explains after Jesus' ascension that Judas "was counted among us and had shared in this ministry" ([ref:Apg 1:16-17|Acts 1:16-17]), confirming that Judas belonged to the circle of the twelve, as Luke emphasizes here.
In [ref:Joh 13:2|John 13:2] it says that the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas, Simon's son Iscariot, to betray Jesus. This shows Satan's active role behind the betrayal.
After the piece of bread "Satan entered him" ([ref:Joh 13:27|John 13:27]). John describes the same phenomenon as Luke – that Satan took control of Judas to carry out the betrayal against Jesus.
